title: Lineage-aware SLO crediting and metric normalization for multi-tenant analytics pipeline
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
The analytics ingest and downstream pipelines currently produce SLIs that are noisy for tenants with low request volumes and biased for workloads that emit large batched events. This causes two practical problems: (1) SLO alerts and dashboards are dominated by high-volume tenants, masking regressions that affect small but critical customers; (2) our trace sampling and billing-sensitive telemetry cost allocation is inaccurate because we double-count events reconciled across replay paths and deduped ingest.

Goal:
Design and implement a lineage-aware SLO crediting and metric normalization layer that: (a) attributes SLI and SLO credit at the ingest lineage granularity (request -> partial events -> aggregated records), (b) normalizes histograms and rates across tenant activity ranges so small tenants surface regressions, and (c) produces an ingest-level weight map to drive cost-aware trace sampling and retention decisions.

Success criteria:
- Per-tenant SLI dashboards show actionable p50/p90/p99 latency and success-rate signals with reduced false positives for tenants < 0.1% of traffic.
- Incident noise from analytics SLOs reduced by >= 30% for the first-month rollout window (measured against baseline).
- Trace sampling decisions use lineage weights and reduce analytics telemetry cost by >= 15% while preserving detection of regressions for tenants with medium+ importance tags.

Design approach (high level):
1) Lineage tokens: augment ingest with a compact lineage token propagated through the pipeline (event-level UUID + ingest-hash). This token enables deduplication and attribution without exposing PII.
2) Attribution windowing: credit successes/failures to a tenant over sliding windows with reservoir-based normalization so spikes from bursty tenants don't overshadow low-volume tenants.
3) Histogram normalization: implement a lightweight per-tenant histogram normalization step that rescales percentiles using a Bayesian shrinkage technique to reduce variance for small-sample tenants.
4) Weight map: compute a per-tenant and per-route weight used by the sampler to increase retention for tenants flagged as high-impact or anomalous while lowering retention for noisy bulk tenants.
5) Backwards-compatible metrics: produce both raw metrics (unchanged) and normalized metrics (new metric names prefixed analytics.norm.) so existing dashboards/alerts can be migrated gradually.

Trade-offs we considered:
- Cost vs fidelity: More aggressive lineage metadata increases payload size and CPU work in the ingest hot path. We limit payload to a 12-byte token and memoize lineage resolution in the pipeline's cache to keep overhead <2% p50 latency.
- Complexity vs adoption: Bayesian normalization gives better small-tenant stability but is more complex to reason about for product owners. We attach explainability metadata to metrics and provide an opt-out label per-tenant.

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (canary): integrate lineage token generation + store minimal lineage index for 5% of tenants (chosen across percentiles) and produce analytics.norm.* metrics. Monitor delta between raw vs normalized SLI signals. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (expand): enable normalization and weight map for 25% of traffic, wire sampling decisions to sampler service for those tenants. Add dashboards and runbook entries. (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (full): server-side flag to toggle for all tenants; update alerting to use normalized signals by default for internal runbooks, keep raw as fallback. (2 weeks)

Operational hooks and dashboards:
- New dashboards: "Normalized SLI Overview", "Lineage Index Coverage", "Sampler Weight Distribution".
- Runbooks: attach standardized playbooks for false-positive SLOs and lineage index reconciliation.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Metrics will be emitted under analytics.norm.*; existing alerts remain on analytics.* until PM/SL owner signs off.
- Provide a migration document with mapping rules and example queries (see attachments).
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Kapoor: Drafted spec after sync with product. Listed initial success criteria and trade-offs. Open questions: retention budget for lineage index and privacy review for ingest token. Filing security review separately if required.

2026-03-03 - Jonah Ruiz: Implemented lineage token generator prototype in ingest-proxy. Microbenchmarks: +1.4% p50 serving latency at 95th percentile load with token memoization enabled. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-proxy/pull/412

2026-03-05 - Data Eng review (L. Chen): Proposed alternative: use existing request_id + checksum instead of new token to avoid schema churn. We decided to keep a separate token for stronger dedupe guarantees and shorter key size.
2026-03-08 - PM review (R. Mendes): PM requested ability to opt tenants into normalized metrics and to annotate exemptions for compliance customers. Added tenant opt-out flag to design.

2026-03-11 - Jonah Ruiz: Completed normalization library prototype (go) and ran backtests on 30 days of staging ingest. False-positive SLO alerts dropped ~34% in staging for small tenants. Data attached in results CSV.

2026-03-12 - Security (S. Patel): Confirmed lineage token design does not include PII and recommended HMAC with short-lived key rotation for the token generation. Security review passed; no blocking issues.
